title: A Science Fiction Book Wins the Booker Prize for the First Time
summary:
For the first time ever, a science fiction book has won the Booker Prize. M. John Harrison's The End of Everything won the 2026 prize. The Booker Prize is one of the most famous awards for books written in English and published in the United Kingdom or Ireland.

The win crowns Harrison's 60-year career. His first short story came out in 1966. He is seen as one of the most original voices in British fantasy and science fiction.

The book is set on England's south coast after a strange disaster. Its hero, Philip Tennent, moved from London to the small town of Dalston-on-Sea. London was taken over by strange, short-lived beings called the iGhetti. Nobody knows if they are really aliens. Tennent earns money by finding alien objects on the beach and selling them. Then something stranger appears: a baby-like creature that keeps growing and learning. Tennent and his aunt Marnie just want to get rid of it.

In 2007, Harrison won the Arthur C. Clarke Award and the Philip K. Dick Award for his book Nova Swing.
why_it_matters: It shows that the stories you love, like tales about aliens and strange worlds, can win the biggest book prizes too.
